newsitem.title: ITALY: Budget scrutiny resumes amid acrimony in Italy.
newsitem.headline: Budget scrutiny resumes amid acrimony in Italy.

text.p: Italy's Chamber of Deputies (lower house) resumed examination of the draft 1997 budget law on Friday amid acrimony between the rival blocs over how far the government could go in bypassing parliament on policy.

The full house, has until November 14 to ratify the package, crucial to Prime Minister Romano Prodi's hopes of taking Italy into Europe's single currency, and is now voting on the draft article by article.
Examination resumed on Friday at article 25, which covers disability pensions, but the chamber has temporarily set aside its scrutiny of other controversial articles.
They cover areas in which the centre-left government has asked for proxy powers, while the centre-right opposition bloc wants the requests to be dropped.
The proxy powers would allow the government to dictate policy on several sensitive budget areas, including on tax, without needing subsequent parliamentary approval.

Prime Minister Romano Prodi has said he is ready to forego some of the requests, though not on tax, but opposition Freedom Alliance leader Silvio Berlusconi rejected the offer late on Thursday as inadequate.

The heat of the issue was raised when Berlusconi hinted at a news conference that his coalition may hold a plan for constitutional reform which requires broad support hostage to the issue unless the centre-left gave ground.

Parliament's work will halt on Saturday because the centre-right has called a demonstration in Rome to protest against the package of measures, but will resume on Sunday when the proxy powers row may be addressed.

The budget aims to slash 62.5 trillion lire ($41 billion) from the public deficit next year to try to lower the deficit ratio to Gross Domestic Product (GDP) to the three percent level set for membership of European economic and monetary union.
Once the lower house has ratified the whole bill, it must pass to the Senate (upper house) for approval.
